# Time, rulers, and snap

Blue arranges the [Score](score.qmd) in musical beats, but time fields can be
entered and displayed in several formats. Three choices serve different jobs:
the **time base** of a position or duration, the **ruler format** shown on
screen, and the **snap value** used when moving or drawing material. You can
change one without necessarily changing the others.

## Positions and durations

A position answers _where?_; a duration answers _how long?_. A SoundObject's
**Start Time** is a position. Its **Subjective Duration** and optional
**Repeat Point** are durations. A marker or tempo point also has a position.

Select a SoundObject and open [Score Object Properties](soundobjects.qmd) to
edit its time fields. Each field has a format menu above the value. Choose the
format, enter the value, then press **Enter** or leave the field to apply it.
Changing a field's format displays its current location or length in that
format. The AudioClip editor similarly separates the clip's Score **Start
Time** and **Duration** from its position within the audio file (**File
Start**).

| Format  | Example entry                                             |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Beats   | `12.5` beats.                                             |
| BBT     | `3.1.0`: bar 3, beat 1, tick 0.                           |
| BBST    | `5.3.2.60`: bar, beat, sixteenth, ticks.                  |
| BBF     | `5.3.50`: bar, beat, hundredths of a beat.                |
| Time    | `0:01:23.450`: hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds.     |
| Seconds | `83.45`: decimal seconds.                                 |
| SMPTE   | `00:01:23:12`: hours, minutes, seconds, frames.           |
| Samples | `4000000`: sample-frame count at the project sample rate. |

Bar-based positions depend on the project's time signature map. A bar-based
duration is a length, not an absolute bar number: a **BBT** position of
`3.1.0` means the start of bar 3, while a **BBT** duration of `1.0.0` means
one bar. Clock and sample displays also depend on the project's tempo and
sample-rate context. The same event can therefore have several useful
representations.

New SoundObjects and AudioClips store their start and duration in beats by
default. The archived Java manual's **Quick Time** dialog and status readout
are not present in the Blue 3 Score workbench; use the field format menus and
toolbar displays instead.

## Set the Score ruler

In the Score toolbar, click **Ruler**. Choose a **Primary Ruler** format and,
if useful, enable a **Secondary Ruler** in another format. The dialog also
sets the ruler's SMPTE frame rate. For example, keep bars and beats on the
primary ruler and clock time on the secondary ruler while lining up music with
a cue. New markers use the primary ruler's time base.

The dialog has **Update ScoreObjects** and **Update Markers** checkboxes.
Both are selected, with **Update All TimeBases**, when the dialog opens. If
you only want a new display, clear both before clicking **OK**. To convert
existing ScoreObjects and markers to the new primary time base, keep both
selected and choose a mode for each:

- **Update All TimeBases** converts their time fields regardless of their
  current time base.
- **Update Matching TimeBases** converts only fields already using the old
  primary ruler's time base. A SoundObject's start, duration, and repeat point
  are checked independently, so one field can change while another keeps its
  original time base.

This distinction matters when some objects use beats and others use seconds.
The ruler controls how you view the Score; the conversion choices control
whether existing objects and markers change their time bases. To convert
ScoreObjects without converting markers, clear **Update Markers**. To convert
only markers, clear **Update ScoreObjects** and leave **Update Markers**
selected.

The ScoreObject conversion visits objects directly on the root Score. It
converts a PolyObject's own start, duration, and repeat point when that
PolyObject is on the root Score, but does not descend into its child layers.
Open a nested PolyObject and inspect its children's time bases separately
after changing the root ruler.

SMPTE text entry in Score Object Properties and the Markers panel uses the
project's selected physical frame rate and counting mode, matching the rulers
and transport. Choose the **SMPTE Format** in Ruler Configuration: 29.97 and
59.94 each have separate **(NDF)** and **(DF)** options. Other rates, such as
**24 fps**, use NDF. One selection sets both rate and counting mode.
Project Defaults supplies the pair for new projects without changing opened projects.

Right-click **Playhead**, then choose **Primary → SMPTE** or
**Secondary → SMPTE** to select the same format options. When the readout is explicitly set to SMPTE, the submenu checks the
current project format. Selecting an option changes the project format as an
undoable action and switches that readout to SMPTE. **Sync to Primary Ruler**
and **Sync to Secondary Ruler** remain available.

Fractional aliases use exact rates: 23.976 is 24000/1001, 29.97 is 30000/1001,
and 59.94 is 60000/1001 frames per elapsed second. NDF counts every frame using
`HH:MM:SS:FF`; its labels differ from clock time. At 29.97 NDF, 60 elapsed seconds
shows `00:00:59:28`, and `00:01:00:00` means 60.060 elapsed seconds.

DF uses `HH:MM:SS;FF` and omits labels, without dropping audio or media frames.
At 29.97 DF, `00:00:59;29` advances to `00:01:00;02`; every tenth minute keeps
frame zero, so `00:09:59;29` advances to `00:10:00;00`. At 59.94 DF, non-tenth
minutes omit labels 00–03 instead. Enter the matching separator; omitted labels
and invalid fields are rejected with validation feedback.

Blue retains elapsed hours beyond 23, such as `25:00:00;00`, without wrapping.
These extended labels are a timeline convention, not a 24-hour wire address.
Durations count frames from zero; calculate differences using elapsed time rather
than subtracting printed label components. Changing format, saving, reopening,
undoing, or redoing it preserves stored positions and durations. Frame snapping
uses physical frame starts through the tempo map and is identical in DF and NDF.
Audio **Sample Frames** continues to use the audio sample rate.

Counting follows [SMPTE ST 12-1:2014](https://pub.smpte.org/latest/st12-1/st0012-1-2014.pdf).

For Score
positions, durations, and marker positions, clock
formats use the project's tempo points, including later tempo changes, when
tempo mapping is enabled. When it is disabled, beats and seconds convert
one-to-one. This does not affect an AudioClip's file-relative **File Start**.
The read-only **End Time** uses the selected **Start Time** format.

## Set snap independently

Click the **Snap** button to turn snapping on or off. Open its adjacent menu
to choose a division. Blue offers bars and musical subdivisions, triplets,
time intervals, SMPTE frames, samples, and **Auto**. Snapping affects where a
dragged object lands; it does not change the ruler's display format. You can,
for example, display seconds while snapping to sixteenths.

The [PianoRoll](piano-roll.qmd) has its own Snap control. Its **Ruler** dialog
can follow the global Score ruler or show local primary and secondary formats.
Changing that view does not rewrite PianoRoll note starts merely to change the
labels.

## Tempo and meter

Use **Project → Edit Tempo Map...** to place or edit tempo points, and
**Project → Edit Time Signature Map...** for meter changes. Tempo determines
how beat positions map to elapsed time; meter determines bar boundaries and
bar-based formatting. If an object must stay aligned to a clock cue when
tempo changes, inspect its time base in Score Object Properties rather than
assuming that a ruler choice controls its timing.

For the difference between an object's displayed width and its generated
notes, see [SoundObjects](soundobjects.qmd). For nested timelines, see
[PolyObjects](polyobjects.qmd).
